turns.assessment: The approximately 5.5 dB loss is confined to och116 at its S08 receiver. Upstream line monitors and amplifier powers did not move, while other S08 channels remained normal, localizing the loss after the incoming OMS monitor and to this channel's ROADM path at S08. A per-channel WSS attenuation drift best fits; receiver degradation is less likely because pre-FEC BER and other receiver-quality metrics did not change.

proposals.rationale: A channel-selective attenuation increase in the S08 ROADM can reduce och116 power at trx.och116.a without changing upstream OCM or amplifier measurements. The lack of changes on other channels argues against an OMS, span, or amplifier fault.
proposals.note: site named; resolved to its node equipment

proposals.rationale: A receiver-local fault could produce anomalous local readings while the optical path remains normal, but the unchanged pre-FEC BER and lack of other receiver penalties make it less likely.
A channel-specific WSS fault is topologically plausible, but filter shift is documented to reduce quality with normal power, contrary to the observed 5.49 dB received-power loss.

clarify.assessment: och116’s signal arriving at trx.och116.a at S08 follows the reverse optical route from S21 through S06–S11–S12–S01–S20, so it enters S08 on degree oms.S20-S08. Therefore the implicated S08 ROADM channel location is oms.S20-S08|8.
